chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Sulayman al-Ja'fari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:
The peacock — it is not permissible to eat it, nor its eggs.

key_terms.الطَّاوُس: Peacock (tawus) — the bird being ruled upon as haram
key_terms.بَيْض: Eggs — also included in the prohibition alongside the bird itself
key_terms.يَحِلُّ: To be permissible/lawful (yahillu) — the legal category of halal

ai.seo_question: Is eating peacock meat and eggs permissible (halal) in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) issued a clear legal ruling prohibiting the consumption of peacock meat and peacock eggs. This ruling is transmitted through a chain including Sulayman al-Ja'fari, a known companion of the Imam. The prohibition extends both to the bird itself and its eggs, establishing a comprehensive dietary restriction.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Suleyman Al Ja’fary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
The peacock, it is not Permissible to eat it nor its eggs’.
en.sarwar: 9. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Bakr ibn Salih from Sulayman ibn Ja‘far who has said the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about peacock.
He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not lawful to use it or its eggs for food.’”
